barbell-bench-press: Lie back with your eyes under the bar and your feet flat on the floor.
Pull your shoulder blades together and keep them pinned to the bench.
Lower the bar under control to your mid-chest, elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Press the bar up until your arms are straight without bouncing it off your chest.
incline-dumbbell-press: Set the bench to a 30 to 45 degree incline and sit with your back firmly against it.
Start with the dumbbells at chest level, wrists stacked over your elbows.
Press up and slightly inward until your arms are straight.
Lower slowly until you feel a stretch in your chest.
chest-fly: Keep a slight bend in your elbows and hold it fixed throughout the movement.
Open your arms wide until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Squeeze your chest to bring the weights together in a wide arc.
Keep your shoulder blades back and avoid using too heavy a weight.
push-up: Place your hands slightly wider than your shoulders and form a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your hips do not sag.
Lower your chest to just above the floor with your elbows at about 45 degrees.
Push the floor away until your arms are fully straight.
deadlift: Stand with the bar over mid-foot and grip it just outside your legs.
Keep your back neutral, chest up and lats tight before you pull.
Push the floor away with your legs while the bar stays close to your body.
Lock out by squeezing your glutes, then lower the bar under control.
pull-up: Hang from the bar with a grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Start by pulling your shoulder blades down, then drive your elbows toward your hips.
Pull until your chin clears the bar without swinging.
Lower yourself slowly to a full hang.
barbell-row: Hinge at the hips with a flat back until your torso is roughly 45 degrees to the floor.
Grip the bar just outside your knees and let it hang with straight arms.
Pull the bar toward your lower ribs, leading with your elbows.
Lower under control without rounding your back or jerking your torso.
lat-pulldown: Sit with your thighs secured under the pads and grip the bar slightly wider than your shoulders.
Lean back slightly and keep your chest up.
Pull the bar to your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back.
Return slowly until your arms are fully extended.
overhead-press: Hold the bar at shoulder height with your grip just outside your shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your core so you do not arch your lower back.
Press the bar straight up, moving your head back slightly to let it pass.
Lock out overhead with the bar over mid-foot, then lower it under control.
lateral-raise: Stand tall with a slight bend in your elbows and the dumbbells at your sides.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they reach about shoulder height.
Lead with your elbows and avoid shrugging your shoulders.
Lower slowly and do not swing your body to lift the weights.
face-pull: Set the cable at upper-chest to face height and use a rope attachment.
Pull the rope toward your face, spreading the ends apart as you go.
Keep your elbows high and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly with a light weight and no leaning back.
arnold-press: Start with the dumbbells in front of your chest, palms facing you.
Press up while rotating your palms to face forward.
Finish with your arms straight overhead without arching your back.
Reverse the rotation as you lower the weights under control.
barbell-curl: Stand tall with your elbows pinned close to your sides.
Curl the bar up by bending only at the elbows.
Squeeze your biceps at the top without swinging your torso.
Lower slowly until your arms are fully extended.
dumbbell-curl: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand and your elbows close to your sides.
Curl the weights up, rotating your palms to face your shoulders.
Keep your upper arms still and your shoulders relaxed.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
hammer-curl: Hold the dumbbells with your palms facing each other.
Keep your elbows tucked at your sides throughout the movement.
Curl the weights up without twisting your wrists.
Lower slowly and avoid swinging your torso.
preacher-curl: Adjust the seat so your upper arms rest flat on the pad.
Curl the weight up without lifting your elbows off the pad.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.
Stop just short of locking out to keep tension off your elbows.
triceps-pushdown: Stand close to the cable with your elbows pinned to your sides.
Push the handle down until your arms are fully straight.
Keep your upper arms still so only your forearms move.
Return slowly until your forearms are just past parallel to the floor.
skull-crusher: Lie on a bench with your arms straight up over your shoulders.
Bend only at the elbows to lower the weight toward your forehead or just behind your head.
Keep your elbows pointing forward and not flaring out.
Extend your arms back up without moving your upper arms.
close-grip-bench-press: Grip the bar about shoulder-width apart, no narrower.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your body as you lower the bar.
Touch your lower chest lightly, then press up powerfully.
Keep your wrists straight and your shoulder blades pinned back.
overhead-triceps-extension: Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands and your elbows pointing forward.
Lower the weight behind your head by bending only at the elbows.
Keep your core braced and avoid arching your back.
Extend your arms fully to return to the top.
back-squat: Set the bar on your upper back and brace your core before you unrack.
Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and toes slightly out.
Sit down and back, keeping your knees tracking over your toes and your chest up.
Descend to at least parallel, then drive up through your whole foot.
front-squat: Rest the bar on your front shoulders with your elbows high.
Keep your torso upright and your core braced.
Squat down with your knees tracking over your toes.
Drive up while keeping your elbows high so the bar stays in place.
leg-press: Place your feet about shoulder-width apart in the middle of the platform.
Keep your lower back and hips flat against the pad.
Lower the sled until your knees reach about 90 degrees.
Press up without locking out your knees completely.
leg-extension: Adjust the seat so your knees line up with the machine pivot.
Extend your legs until they are straight, squeezing your quads at the top.
Keep your hips down and avoid swinging the weight.
Lower slowly rather than letting the weight drop.
romanian-deadlift: Stand with the bar at hip height and your knees slightly bent.
Push your hips back while keeping the bar close to your legs.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings, keeping your back flat.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.
lying-leg-curl: Lie face down with the pad just above your heels.
Curl your heels toward your glutes without lifting your hips.
Squeeze your hamstrings at the top.
Lower slowly until your legs are almost straight.
good-morning: Place the bar on your upper back and soften your knees slightly.
Push your hips back and hinge forward with a flat back.
Lower until your torso is near parallel to the floor or you feel a hamstring stretch.
Drive your hips forward to stand up, using a light weight.
seated-leg-curl: Adjust the machine so your knees line up with its pivot and the pad rests above your heels.
Curl the pad down and back by bending your knees.
Keep your back against the seat and squeeze at the bottom.
hip-thrust: Rest your upper back on a bench with the bar across your hips.
Place your feet flat about hip-width apart, with your shins vertical at the top.
Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips.
Keep your chin tucked and avoid over-arching your lower back.
bulgarian-split-squat: Rest your rear foot on a bench behind you and step your front foot forward.
Keep your torso upright and your front foot flat.
Lower straight down until your front thigh is about parallel to the floor.
Push through your front heel to stand back up.
walking-lunge: Take a long step forward and keep your torso upright.
Lower until both knees are bent to about 90 degrees.
Keep your front knee over your ankle and not caving inward.
Push off the front foot to step into the next lunge.
glute-bridge: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.
Brace your core and press through your heels.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower slowly.
standing-calf-raise: Stand with the balls of your feet on a step or platform.
Rise as high as you can onto your toes.
Pause briefly at the top to squeeze your calves.
Lower slowly until you feel a full stretch.
seated-calf-raise: Sit with the pads resting on your lower thighs and the balls of your feet on the platform.
Lower your heels to get a full stretch in your calves.
Press up through your toes as high as you can.
Pause at the top and lower slowly.
donkey-calf-raise: Hinge forward at the hips with the balls of your feet on a raised step.
Keep your legs straight and your back flat.
Rise as high as you can onto your toes.
Lower slowly into a deep stretch.
leg-press-calf-raise: Sit in the leg press with only the balls of your feet on the lower edge of the platform.
Extend your legs without fully locking your knees.
Press through your toes as far as you can.
Lower slowly to feel a full calf stretch.
plank: Place your forearms on the floor with your elbows under your shoulders.
Form a straight line from your head to your heels.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your hips do not sag or rise.
Breathe steadily and keep your neck neutral.
hanging-leg-raise: Hang from a bar with your shoulders pulled down and your body still.
Raise your legs by curling your pelvis up, not just swinging your legs.
Lift until your legs are at least parallel to the floor.
cable-crunch: Kneel below a high cable with the rope held beside your head.
Curl your ribs toward your hips by flexing your spine.
Keep your hips still rather than sitting back.
Return slowly while keeping tension on your abs.
ab-wheel-rollout: Kneel with the wheel under your shoulders and your core braced.
Roll forward slowly while keeping your back flat.
Go only as far as you can without your hips sagging.
Pull the wheel back by contracting your abs.
